A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NDM research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original toy-model experiments, GPT-2 circuit evaluations, qualitative subspace analyses, and knowledge-conflict experiments on Qwen2.5-1.5B and Gemma-2-2B.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds SAE-derived baseline results and a stricter-threshold qualitative analysis.

M1.justification: NDM's orthogonal transformation, nearest-neighbor objective, MI-based merging and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. The toy-setting heuristics and alternative approaches are also retained. The new SAE extraction procedure serves as a comparator, not a modification of NDM.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic feature settings, MiniPile/OpenWebText data, IOI and Greater-than tasks, and RAVEL Nobel-prize knowledge-conflict scenarios. The SAE comparison uses the existing GPT-2 test suite; the additional positional examples retain existing inputs and task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds the Feature comparator, which constructs subspaces from SAE feature clusters using an adaptation of Engels et al. (2024), across all five GPT-2 tests. This introduces a substantive comparison beyond the retained Identity, Random, PCA 1 and PCA 2 controls. The larger-model comparator sets are unchanged.

E3.justification: The added SAE evaluation introduces clustering/extraction parameter searches and filters restricting resulting partitions to 5–50 subspaces. Figure 31 additionally evaluates preimages at cosine similarity 0.99. Existing NDM training settings, intervention procedures, sample counts and Gini metrics are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix F.2 compares SAE clustering and extraction configurations and reports graph-clustering variants failing the partition constraints. Figure 31 adds evidence about positional precision under a stricter similarity threshold. Existing NDM ablations, qualitative cases and alternative-method analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, seed counts, confidence intervals or formal significance tests. The retained activation-variance normalization and averaging over evaluation examples do not constitute new uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1 and 8 add substantial SAE comparison results across all five GPT-2 tests: the best average Gini coefficient is 0.56, while NDM's retained score is 0.71. Table 5 adds resulting subspace counts, and Figure 31 adds stricter-threshold preimages. The positional caption in v1 Figure 22(a), now Figure 23(a), is corrected from 118 to 117.

T1.justification: Appendix F.2 adds a formal orthogonalization construction for the SAE comparator, defining residual reconstructions as X - CC^T X before SVD-based subspace selection. The original entropy/total-correlation reasoning, intervention and Gini definitions, and alternative-objective formulations remain unchanged; no new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same contributions: unsupervised discovery of interpretable subspaces, alignment with circuit variables, applicability to approximately 2B models, and potential subspace circuits. The new comparisons support these claims without materially redefining their scope.

C2.justification: The new SAE discussion explains difficulties with patching mutually exclusive individual features and interprets InversionView as analogous to a parameter-free top-1 SAE. Figure 31 newly attributes residual positional errors to imperfect optimization or partial loss of position information. Existing applicability and interpretability limitations are largely retained.

D1.justification: Appendix F.2 newly documents the comparator's clustering procedures, cluster ordering, orthogonalization, SVD thresholds, parameter grids and exclusion rules. Existing NDM hyperparameters, hardware and timing disclosures, and code/database access information remain available.

R1.justification: Appendix F adds focused positioning relative to SAEs and makes Engels et al. (2024) an explicitly adapted empirical comparator. It also discusses connections to top-1 SAEs. The cited-work set and broader positioning around unsupervised subspace discovery are unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized explanatory and language edits, condenses the main discussion, and moves much of the future-directions discussion to Appendix G.3. It adds the SAE discussion and an LLM-use disclosure. Most prose and the overall research narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the decomposition schematic in Figure 2, the threshold comparison in Figure 31, and Table 8. It annotates the main preimage panels and expands Tables 1 and 5. Most existing graphics are preserved, with relocation, renumbering and ICLR-template reformatting.

improvement.justification: The SAE-derived comparator supplies a more relevant empirical challenge than v1's generic rotation/PCA controls, strengthening comparative support on the existing test suite. The schematic, annotations, subspace counts and threshold example also make the evidence easier to assess. These are useful but limited gains: the central findings remain unchanged, and Appendix F.2 leaves the SAE checkpoint and training setup unspecified, limiting reproducibility of the new comparison.
